geometry_edits.rationale: Transform the dominant cantilever into a split-wing mass so the access edge can become a real public void instead of a closed wedge.
Split along the short axis to open the frontage-directed void.
Increase the separation enough to read as a usable court or entry seam.
Preserve a clean anchor at grade so the mass remains coherent and not overly fragmented.
Lower the ground connector to reinforce public threshold continuity.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the single cantilever gesture with a split-wing logic to open a clearer ground threshold and make the public void legible at the access edge.
Widen the central gap so the mass produces a more public court/entry seam instead of a sealed wedge.
Keep a grounded connecting bar so the composition remains one dominant mass with hierarchy rather than fragmenting into separate objects.
Make the base connector slim enough to preserve open space while still reading as a clean anchor.
Lower the spine so the ground response reads as public and traversable rather than as another stacked mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bent-and-cantilevered mass across views, and parcel containment appears respected. However, the public-space figure is weak: the visible void is minimal and not convincingly shaped as a usable court or entry threshold. The primary road frontage/access edge is answered mostly by a sealed/sloped solid rather than a legible public ground response, which conflicts with the neighborhood-living brief. The silhouette is not broken, but the section feels more like an object pile-up than a mixed-use building with an active base. References 1-3 support courtyard/public-threshold thinking; 4 is a partial podium lesson only; 5 is counterfactual and should be used only as a transferable spanning/void relation, not as a typology.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact massing with a clear public interior/outdoor threshold and layered upper expression around a void.
Courtyard-centered neighborhood commercial logic with strong enclosure and usable ground-space figure.
Small commercial object with legible street response and simple capacity-aware enclosure.
